'''StatCounter''' is an Irish [[web traffic]] analysis website started in 1999.<ref name="About" /> Access to basic services is free to use and advanced services can cost between {{currency|5|US}} and US$119 a month.<ref name="Twitter for Dummies">{{cite book | title=Twitter Marketing for Dummies | series=--For Dummies | publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]] | location=[[Hoboken, New Jersey]] | author=Lacy, Kyle | page=[https://archive.org/details/twittermarketing0000lacy/page/93 93] | year=2011 | isbn=9780470930571 | url=https://archive.org/details/twittermarketing0000lacy/page/93 }}</ref> StatCounter is based in [[Dublin, Ireland]]. The statistics from StatCounter are used to compute web usage share for example.<ref name="statcounterglobal">{{cite web | url=http://gs.statcounter.com/ | title=StatCounter Global Stats | publisher=StatCounter | access-date=22 August 2012 }}</ref>  {{As of|2019|05}}, StatCounter is used on 0.9% of all websites.<ref name="w3techusage">{{cite web | title=Usage statistics and market share of StatCounter for websites | url=http://w3techs.com/technologies/details/ta-statcounter/all/all | website=W3Techs | publisher=Q-Success | access-date=26 May 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526190033/https://w3techs.com/technologies/details/ta-statcounter/all/all | archive-date=26 May 2019}}</ref>

StatCounter statistics are directly derived from [[Hit (Internet)|hits]]—as opposed to [[Unique user|unique visitors]]—from 3 million sites, which use StatCounter, resulting in total hits of more than 15 billion per month.<ref name="faqmethod">{{cite web | url=http://gs.statcounter.com/faq#methodology | title=FAQ | at=What methodology is used to calculate StatCounter Global Stats? | website=StatCounter | access-date=8 January 2015 }}</ref> No artificial weightings are used to correct for [[sampling bias]], thus the numbers in the statistics can not be considered to be [[representative sample]]s.

The company was founded by Aodhán Cullen at the age of 16. Cullen received the "Internet Hero" award at the 2008 Eircom [[Golden Spider Awards]].<ref>{{cite news | work=TechCentral.ie | publisher=[[ComputerScope#MediaTeam|MediaTeam]] | date=21 November 2008 | url=http://www.techcentral.ie/article.aspx?id=12820 | title=eircom Golden Spiders announced | url-status=dead | archive-date=19 November 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101119064451/http://www.techcentral.ie/article.aspx?id=12820 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.leemunroe.com/golden-spider-awards-2008-winners/ | at=Internet Hero | access-date=8 January 2015 | title=Golden Spider Awards 2008 Winners | date=November 2008 | author=Munroe, Lee | type=blog }}</ref> He was also named the 2007 ''[[Bloomberg Businessweek|BusinessWeek]]'' "Young European Entrepreneur of the Year".<ref>{{cite news | author=Reinhardt, Andy | author2=Schenker, Jennifer L. | title=Europe's Young Entrepreneurs 2007 | department=Global Economics | work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] | date=1 June 2007 | url=http://www.businessweek.com/stories/2007-06-01/europes-young-entrepreneurs-2007businessweek-business-news-stock-market-and-financial-advice | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024043450/http://www.businessweek.com/stories/2007-06-01/europes-young-entrepreneurs-2007businessweek-business-news-stock-market-and-financial-advice | url-status=dead | archive-date=24 October 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siliconrepublic.com/careers/item/8521-the-friday-interview-aodha|title=The Friday interview: Aodhan Cullen, StatCounter|author=John Kennedy|work=Silicon Republic |publisher=siliconrepublic.com|date=3 August 2007|access-date=21 September 2012}}</ref>
